title: Customer Security Concern Router and Exception Calculator
creator: Asha Nair
description: Problem: Enterprise sales and customer success receive a growing volume of security and compliance asks (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA questions, vendor questionnaires). Current intake is ad-hoc: many tickets land in email or Slack, triage time is inconsistent, and engineers spend time answering low-impact asks. We need an automated router and 'exception calculator' so that each request is scored, routed, and provided with a recommended response path and SLAs.
goals: Reduce time-to-initial-response for high-risk security asks to <24 hours.
Automatically classify and route 70% of incoming questionnaires to the appropriate lane (self-serve docs, security SME, legal/contract) within sprint 1.
Provide deterministic escalation guidance for contract exceptions and regulatory scope asks using a transparent risk model.
scope_included: Structured intake form (web + Slack shortcut) capturing key signals: compliance type, data residency, PHI/PII presence, urgency, customer tier, contractual ask.
Scoring model that computes a triage score from weighted signals and maps to lanes: self-serve, security SME, legal review, sales-engaged workaround.

Exception Calculator: maps contractual exception asks (e.g., data processing location, retention, sub-processing) to a risk band (low/medium/high) with suggested approval paths and templated responses.
Dashboard for PM/Security showing queue sizes, SLA attainment, and common ask taxonomy.
out_of_scope: Automated fulfillment for complex legal contract renegotiations (these remain human-handled).
Full replacement of the SOC2/ISO audit evidence collection flow (this is a separate project).
triage_model_spec_summary: Inputs: compliance_type, contains_phi, contains_pii, data_location, customer_tier, revenue_signal, contract_clause_flags, urgency_flag, previous_request_count. Weights: compliance_type 30%, contains_phi 20%, data_location 15%, customer_tier 10%, contract_clause_flags 15%, urgency 10%. Score bands: 0-29 (self-serve), 30-59 (security SME + templated response), 60-84 (security+legal review), 85-100 (exec escalation & Dedicated sales involvement). The model must be interpretable and stored as a rule-set (not opaque ML) for auditability.
exception_calculator_logic: Rule engine that scores each exception clause by severity and compensating controls. Each clause is mapped to: severity (1-5), allowed_alternatives (list), required_approvers (security, legal, sales). Final exception risk = weighted sum of clause severities - compensating control score. Risk band threshold determines sign-off path. All decisions and rationale are logged for audit.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form: captures all required signals and returns a triage ticket with computed triage_score for >95% of submissions.
Router: 70% of incoming requests within pilot customers are auto-routed to the correct lane with no manual reassignment in Week 2 of pilot.
SLA: High-risk requests show initial assignment within 24 hours and 90th percentile assignment time <12 hours across pilot.
Exception calculator: produces a suggested sign-off path and response template for 90% of standard clause asks, with an audit log entry for each decision.
success_metrics: Mean time to first assignment for high-risk asks reduced from baseline to <24 hours.
% auto-routing accuracy compared to manual baseline >= 70% in pilot.
Reduction in engineer hours spent on low-impact asks by 40% in quarter after launch.
Number of contract exceptions that require executive approval reduced by 25% via compensating controls automation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): 4-week pilot with SalesOps and two enterprise customers; Phase 2: expand to all Sales/SRE/Support queues and add Slack intake shortcuts; Phase 3: integrate with Console SSO and audit logs. Monitor KPIs in dashboard; freeze changes during customer-facing pilot week. Training docs and templated responses to be published to Drive before Phase 1 kick-off.
implementation_notes: Prototype router behavior as a ruleset written in YAML, executed by the intake service (no ML blackbox) for auditability.
Use existing Redwood Console auth and customer metadata APIs to enrich intake signals (customer_tier, active_contracts, regions).
Design to emit structured events for downstream automation (Slack notifications, Zendesk ticket creation, Github issue linking).
Plan for feature flag gating to gradually roll out triage logic per customer or org.
open_questions: What threshold of revenue or ARR do we consider 'enterprise' for the customer_tier weight?
Should the router allow customers to override the recommended lane, and if so, how will that be tracked?
What is the escalation SLA for weekend/holiday submissions?
Who will own tuning the weights over time and the governance for changes?
